overall: The AG found no violation on the recording announcement, but found the Council violated the law by failing to approve minutes in a timely manner and by missing the 14-business-day complaint response deadline. Ordered compliance and approval of the minutes backlog.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council President failed to require people intending to record meetings to notify him at the start of meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, President Cadime properly complied with the law by notifying the public at the beginning of the meeting that the meeting was being recorded.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council, as a practice, does not create and/or approve written meeting minutes in a timely way.
allegations.key_passage: The Council has failed to create and approve meeting minutes in a timely manner, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council did not respond to the Open Meeting Law complaints within 14 business days of receiving them.
allegations.key_passage: By taking nearly four months to respond, the Board clearly failed to comply with the Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
Within 60 days of receipt of the determination, approve the backlog of draft minutes of its meetings held since July 1, 2010.
remedy_passage: Additionally, we order the Council, within 60 days of receipt of this determination, to approve the backlog of draft minutes of its meetings held since July 1, 2010.
